data.title: Chat: an AS-25 guard has the vacuous shape AS-54 was failed for, plus three boundary findings

data.to:
Findings from the AS-54 cycle-2 QA review (qa-ruben, 2026-09-03; verdict PASS 12/12, none blocked the merge). AS-54 merged at d7ed2ae. Two are in apps/chat, one is a pre-existing guard in a file AS-54 never touched, and one is a corpus measurement nobody had made.

1. A GUARD IN AS-25's TEST CARRIES THE EXACT SHAPE AS-54 WAS FAILED FOR. api.test.js around line 657 asserts a property by naming an anchor and then running an unbounded lazy match across the rest of the served file. The reviewer demonstrated it: adding one extra call of a similar shape anywhere below it makes the guard read a wrong value as the asserted one, and the suite stays green with the behaviour regressed. AS-54 was failed and reworked for this exact defect; this instance predates it and lives in a file AS-54 was scoped out of. Fix it the way AS-54's was fixed: bound the assertion to the region it names, and assert the region's COMPLETE contents rather than the presence of one member — bounding alone is insufficient, which AS-54 established by writing the mutation that a bounded-but-lenient guard still passes.

2. A FUZZ ASSERTION IS EXERCISED BY ZERO OF FIFTY THOUSAND INPUTS. AC-6's href-shape assertion never fires, because every generated salt is glued to a chunk and all eleven chunks begin with an alphanumeric character. So the generator cannot produce the input the assertion exists to reject. This is the same gap the plan deliberately closed one character to the left and left open one character to the right. Not fixed during review because changing the generator changes every number that criterion asserts; it needs its own pass with the numbers re-derived.

3. THE EN DASH IS A HIGHER-RISK BOUNDARY CLASS THAN THE ELLIPSIS, AND NOBODY HAD MEASURED IT. The trailing-ellipsis case was filed as backlog on the strength of a corpus measurement; the reviewer re-derived it independently and agreed with the call — 63 occurrences, 52 glued left, but glued to a scheme run exactly once and that one already inside a markdown link, so real exposure is zero. He then measured the class nobody had: U+2013 appears 62 times and is glued left 62 times, a 100 percent glue rate against the ellipsis's 83 percent. The em dash, which two people expected to be the problem, is spaced 954 times out of 955. Decide the boundary treatment for the en dash on that evidence, and decide the ellipsis with it since they are one rule.

4. SEVENTY-ONE INVISIBLE AND FORMAT CODE POINTS ENTER THE HREF. Every one of the 71 the reviewer tested passes the character exclusions, so a link's visible text and its actual target can differ invisibly. No markup escapes and the structure-first property holds, so this is not a rendering defect; it is a display-integrity question about what a person can verify by looking. Decide whether to exclude them, render them visibly, or accept and document the limit.

ALSO RECORDED, cosmetic: the AS-54 plan's corpus histogram in section 3.1 says letters times four and sums to twelve; two reviewers independently measure five and thirteen. Stale number in a merged plan, no consequence.

ACCEPTANCE: items 1 and 2 each have a mutation that reddens the suite where it currently stays green, shown once per the house technique (assert the mutation applied SCOPED TO THE REGION IT EDITS, occurrence-accurate counts never grep -c, predicted executable case names that exist, restore, prove restoration by content hash plus git status --porcelain). Items 3 and 4 are decisions first: state the rule, then the test. Zero new dependencies — apps/chat is deliberately dependency-free and adding a DOM harness is a separate decision. No protected top-level file edited; no running container touched; every suite server on an ephemeral port. Complexity low.

PLANNED (cto-owen, 2026-09-11T05:45Z, third lane of watcher:25355). Correction to where the finding lives: the vacuous guard is the AS-25 client-side guard in test/api.test.js ('the 5s poll is retired') that regex-parses public/app.js — its /setInterval\(([\s\S]*?),\s*([\d_]+)\)/g stops at the first ', <digits>)' after the opener, so a nested setTimeout(fn, 60_000) would be read as the cadence; still true on master 3398238 (AS-99 added render calls to the 15 s body, timer count still exactly two at app.js:1547/1557). Findings 2-4 are the AS-54 autolink tokenizer (public/markdown.js, test/markdown.test.js): (2) still true verbatim at markdown.test.js:254-266 — every SALT is glued to an alnum-leading CHUNK so the first-host-char assertion never fires; (3) decided D3: trailing en dash / em dash / ellipsis are prose, tail-trim only; (4) decided D4: exclude \p{Cf} (u flag) from the URL body, candidate stops at the char, href stays a verbatim slice. AS-72 touches neither server.js nor stream.test.js, so the AS-100 seam is clean; if AS-100's client adds a timer to app.js the new 'exactly two intervals' guard goes red on rebase and the implementer re-derives the region's contents rather than relaxing the count. 9 ACs; AC-1 and AC-4 each record a mutant GREEN under the old test and RED under the new one (that is the vacuity proof). Implementer developer-marcus after AS-61 (Lena takes it if her lane frees first); QA qa-priya (Ruben filed the findings). Branch feat/AS-72-as25-guard-autolink, worktree .worktrees/AS-72. Open in plan §7: the enclosing function name for app.js:1547-1561 and the re-pinned urlTokens count after the generator change — the implementer records both.
